### Description of materials

| Number of credit hours: | Course Title | Article number |
|-------------------------|--------------|-----------------|
| 3                       | Wording Indications and their legal applications | 0406716 |

**Prerequisite:** -0

**The description:**
This article deals with the semantics of words according to fundamentalists. It is exposed according to the Hanafi and Shafi'i schools of thought, dividing the connotations of words in terms of clarity and concealment—the hidden, the problematic, the general, and the similar. It examines how the word denotes the meaning—such as the phrase, the reference, the connotation, the implication, the spoken, and the understood—and its placement of the meaning, such as the general, the specific, and the common. The focus of the study of these topics is on their legal applications. Various legal texts from the Personal Status Law, the Civil Law, and all other legislative areas are presented, interpreted according to the rules of interpretation of texts and their meanings in the science of jurisprudence.

| Number of credit hours: | Course Title | Article number |
|-------------------------|--------------|-----------------|
| 3                       | Research Methods in Jurisprudence and Sharia Judiciary | 0406703 |

**Prerequisite:** -0

**The description:**
This course deals with scientific research in jurisprudence and the judiciary in terms of definition, importance, and comparison between research in jurisprudence and in the judiciary. It addresses how to identify the research problem, its importance and objectives, analysis of previous studies, the limits of the study, and the division of the study into chapters, investigations, demands, and research methods. It covers inductive, descriptive, analytical, and comparative approaches, as well as research sources, global and digital databases in jurisprudence and the judiciary, documentation methods, writing techniques, and training students to prepare integrated research and evaluate research and university theses.
